review_output: {"summary":"I found no BLOCKER or MAJOR issues. The fix holds up: canonical authorization reruns after the source, version and session locks, and identity drift is rejected. I have three lower-confidence MINOR or NIT concerns, all depending on helper or schema details not supplied.","findings":[{"issue":"Every LiveChatError becomes a 403, including possible transient failures from the helper such as rate limiting or an unavailable dependency.","severity":"MINOR","area":"Route error mapping","impact":"Clients may read temporary failures as revoked access and stop collecting metrics. It also hides operational failures behind an authorization response.","confidence":0.4,"recommended_fix":"Map each LiveChatError code explicitly. Only access, credential or moderation codes should return 403; transient codes should return 429 or 503.","evidence":"route.ts: `if (error instanceof LiveChatError) return json({ error: \"Viewer access required\" }, 403);` applies to every LiveChatError, whatever its code.","required_test":"Make the helper throw each non-authorization LiveChatError code during resolve and revalidate, and assert the route returns a non-403 status.","file":"src/app/api/live-metrics/[vendorId]/[liveId]/intervals/route.ts"},{"issue":"The full canonical helper reruns while holding FOR UPDATE on the metric session. If it locks or writes chat-session or blacklist rows, that lock order is new and unverified.","severity":"MINOR","area":"Revalidation lock ordering","impact":"Concurrent moderation or chat flows could deadlock with ingestion. A deadlock only surfaces as a 503 and causes repeated retry churn.","confidence":0.3,"recommended_fix":"Document and assert that the helper is read-only with no row locks, or make any helper locks follow the source-first order before the metric-session lock.","evidence":"`authorization(tx, \"revalidate\")` runs after `FOR UPDATE OF s`. Whether resolveVerifiedPrivateChatViewer takes row locks or writes was not supplied.","required_test":"Run a two-PID test with a moderation or chat transaction locking chat or blacklist rows while ingestion revalidates. Assert no 40P01 and the correct final outcome.","file":"src/lib/live-metric-ingestion.ts"},{"issue":"Expiry checks mix time types: admission compares to `clock_timestamp() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'`, while version and session compare to plain clock_timestamp(). One style gives wrong results if Postgres session TimeZone isn't UTC.","severity":"NIT","area":"Session/version expiry enforcement","impact":"With a non-UTC database or session TimeZone, an expired session or version could still accept writes, or a valid one could be rejected. Only this SQL enforces those expiries.","confidence":0.3,"recommended_fix":"Use the same comparison for every expiry, chosen from the real column types, or pin `SET LOCAL TIME ZONE 'UTC'` inside the transaction.","evidence":"`v.\"expiresAt\">clock_timestamp() AND s.\"expiresAt\">clock_timestamp()` vs `a.\"expiresAt\"> (clock_timestamp() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')`; `r.\"verifiedAt\" AT TIME ZONE 'UTC'` suggests the column types are mixed.","required_test":"Run the real-database expiry tests with session TimeZone set to a non-UTC zone, such as America/New_York. Assert that expired sessions, versions and admissions are rejected at their boundaries.","file":"src/lib/live-metric-ingestion.ts"}]}
